title: Kwem / Kpwem (Cassava Leaves with Ripe Banana and Palm-Nut Juice)
author: Maniguette (cameroun24.net)
desc: A packet of cassava leaves cooked 20 minutes with four finely blended ripe bananas, then a can of palm-nut juice stirred in and cooked 20 more minutes on low heat.
longDesc: The page describes kwem as a cassava-leaf paste much prized among the peoples of the centre of the country (Beti, Bulu, Eton). The bananas are peeled and blended finely. The cassava leaves go in a pot with a glass of water; the banana is added and mixed, and the pot cooks 20 minutes, stirring constantly. The can of palm-nut juice (sauce graine) is poured in and stirred to a uniform mixture, then it cooks 20 more minutes on low heat. Served with cassava or macabo. SAFETY, STATED PLAINLY: the page prints no step for preparing the cassava leaves and no warning about them; elsewhere in this collection the Immaculate Bites cassava leaf page warns that fresh, raw cassava leaves are toxic when eaten raw. The packet’s preparation state is not printed.
ingredients: 1 packet cassava leaves (pack size not printed)
1 can palm-nut juice (sauce graine; can size not printed)
A glass of water (in the method, not the list)
steps: Peel the bananas and blend them finely.
Put the cassava leaves in a pot with a glass of water. Add the banana and mix.
Add the palm-nut juice and stir to a uniform mixture.
Cook another 20 minutes on low heat. Serve with cassava or macabo.
chefTips: Printed cues: ‘en remuant constamment’ and ‘une préparation homogène’.
The page lists 30 minutes of preparation and 1 hour of cooking but its steps add up to 40 minutes of cooking.
Use leaves already prepared as the pack states; the page gives no preparation or warning.
commonMistakes: Eating cassava leaves that have not been properly cooked.
Not stirring constantly so the banana catches.
Using an unspecified can without tasting for salt.
healthBenefits: Cassava leaves are a leafy green; ripe banana adds natural sugar.
culturalNote: The page says kwem is much prized among the peoples of the centre (Beti, Bulu, Eton). The byline is a handle and the date is shown only as ‘il y a 11 ans’.
sources: Title as printed: ‘La recette du Kwem ou Kpwem’. Byline as printed: ‘Maniguette’ (handle; flagged). Date printed only as ‘il y a 11 ans’ (relative; flagged). Printed times: ‘Préparation : 30 minutes’, ‘Cuisson : 1 heure’; the steps add to 40 minutes of cooking (cook value 40 follows the steps). Yield not printed (servings 4 is a placeholder). TWO-PASS.
SAFETY GAP: no cassava-leaf preparation or toxicity statement on the page. The warning quoted above is from a different page (Immaculate Bites, cassava leaf soup).
